data.one_liner: Annotate Dart objects to serialize and deserialize them from and to JSON.
data.what_it_does: Allows developers to serialize and deserialize Dart objects to and from JSON using annotations. It generates a single mapping file for the entire project via code generation and avoids `dart:mirrors` for cross-platform compatibility.
use_when: You want clean model classes free of manual JSON serialization logic.
You need advanced JSON mapping features like inheritance, polymorphism, and object cloning.
You prefer a single centralized mapping file over per-class generated files.
avoid_when: You prefer the standard Google-backed `json_serializable` approach with per-class generated files.
You want to avoid setting up `build_runner` code generation.
strengths: Keeps model classes clean with no boilerplate serialization methods inside them.
Rich out-of-the-box features like polymorphism, object cloning, and case style conversion.
Generates a single centralized mapper file for the whole project.
weaknesses: Requires running a code generator (`build_runner`) whenever model classes change.
Less common choice in the Dart ecosystem compared to `json_serializable`.
data.setup_notes: Requires adding `build_runner` to dev_dependencies and configuring `build.yaml` to run code generation.

alternatives.name: json_annotation
alternatives.why_pick_it: It is the standard, widely adopted solution from the Dart team which generates per-class `*.g.dart` files.

alternatives.name: built_value
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want immutable value types with built-in serialization and runtime validation.

alternatives.name: freezed_annotation
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want union types, immutable classes, and pattern matching support along with JSON serialization.
